text: Open Source Intel Local media in South Africa and Fiji have named the two flydubai pilots credited with taking control of their aircraft and preventing a mass-casualty attack. Neither the airline nor any official body has confirmed their identities. Acquaintances identified the South African pilot as Rowan Tooth, originally from Kimberley, according to Cape Town Etc. The second pilot, Henson Steven, is from Fiji, not New Zealand as first claimed, and previously flew for Fiji's national airline, a Fijian outlet reported. The details emerged over the weekend, five days after both men received certificates of appreciation for their heroism. Kann. tweet

text: Republican Senator Darline Graham is locked in a tight race against Democrat Annie Andrews in traditionally Republican South Carolina, raising the possibility of a major Democratic upset. Graham, appointed after her brother Lindsey Graham’s death in July, has faced criticism over her political inexperience and weak support among conservatives. A New York Times/Siena poll shows the candidates virtually tied, despite Trump’s repeated campaign appearances. Asked whether she was angry at her brother for putting her in this situation, Graham joked, “When I get to heaven one day, I am just going to choke Lindsey.” Source: NYT
text_zh: 共和党参议员达琳·格雷厄姆（Darline Graham）在传统的共和党票仓南卡罗来纳州与民主党人安妮·安德鲁斯（Annie Andrews）展开了激烈的竞争，这引发了民主党可能爆出重大冷门的猜测。格雷厄姆在其兄长林赛·格雷厄姆（Lindsey Graham）于7月去世后被任命，她因政治经验不足和在保守派中支持率疲软而受到批评。尽管特朗普多次参加竞选活动，但《纽约时报》/锡耶纳学院的民调显示，两位候选人的支持率几乎持平。当被问及是否因兄长让她陷入这种境地而感到愤怒时，格雷厄姆开玩笑说：“等我将来有一天到了天堂，我一定要掐死林赛。”来源：《纽约时报》

text: 🇮🇷 🇺🇸 Rezaei on Vance's letter: "Their tone has completely changed" Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council and former commander of the IRGC, says he has read the letter sent to him by US Vice President JD Vance but hasn't replied yet. "Their tone has completely changed, which is a good sign," he said, adding that the Iranian people have consolidated their victory. According to the Wall Street Journal, Vance sent the letter this week at Trump's direction, in a bid to restart peace talks. Rezaei said no new decision has been made at the government level on negotiations. But he revealed that Tehran is now debating whether, if war breaks out again, Iran should keep its previous doctrine or change it, an apparent reference to its nuclear posture. The public is demanding answers, he said: Iran cooperated fully with IAEA inspections, answered every request and allowed cameras at all its sites, and the enemy still attacked all its nuclear facilities. "So naturally, when people see all of this, their question to us is: Why do you want to continue down the same path?" 🔴 @DDGeopolitics
text_zh: 🇮🇷 🇺🇸 雷扎伊谈万斯的信：“他们的语气完全变了” 伊朗最高国家安全委员会秘书、伊斯兰革命卫队前司令穆赫辛·雷扎伊表示，他已经读了美国副总统万斯寄给他的信，但尚未回复。“他们的语气完全变了，这是一个好迹象，”他说，并补充称伊朗人民已经巩固了胜利。据《华尔街日报》报道，万斯是在特朗普的指示下于本周发出这封信的，旨在重启和平谈判。雷扎伊表示，政府层面尚未就谈判做出任何新决定。但他透露，德黑兰目前正在讨论如果战争再次爆发，伊朗是应保持此前的原则还是做出改变，这显然是指其核立场。他说，公众正在要求答案：伊朗完全配合了国际原子能机构的视察，回答了每一个请求，并允许在所有地点安装摄像头，但敌人仍然袭击了其所有核设施。“所以很自然地，当人们看到这一切时，他们对我们的质问是：你们为什么要继续走同样的路？” 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

text: ↩️ Reply to WarFront Witness: "⚡️🇫🇷 Multiple videos from ongoing protests in Paris on October 31 show escalating clashes between demonstrators and police, with an explosive device reportedly igniting near an officer's leg, a Molotov cocktail bursting into flames, and protesters throwing…" ⚡️ 🇫🇷 🇩🇪 🇮🇹 🇪🇸 AP News : Beyond the ongoing demonstrations in France, a wave of youth-led protests is spreading across Europe, with rallies taking place in Germany, Italy, and Spain. Protesters are voicing frustration over rising living costs, housing shortages, education funding, and government policies. In Germany, thousands gathered in Berlin as the "Gen Z regelt" movement organized demonstrations across more than 30 cities, demanding affordable living conditions, improved public services, and opposition to compulsory military service. Italy has also witnessed nationwide demonstrations and strikes, while Spain has experienced renewed unrest. The protests reflect growing dissatisfaction among young Europeans over economic pressures and political decisions. Authorities across several countries have increased security measures following clashes between demonstrators and police, raising concerns about further unrest in the coming days. @wfwitness

text: ⚡️ 🇬🇧 Reuters : British Prime Minister Burnham said he is open to issuing a formal apology for Britain's historical involvement in the transatlantic slave trade, but ruled out paying financial reparations to affected countries. Burnham said Britain would engage in structured dialogue with nations and communities affected by slavery, arguing that today's British population should not be held financially responsible for historical injustices. Instead, he proposed debt relief initiatives to help vulnerable Commonwealth countries secure longer repayment periods and lower interest rates. The announcement comes ahead of next week's Commonwealth summit in Antigua and Barbuda, where Caribbean leaders are expected to renew demands for reparatory justice. Antigua and Barbuda's Prime Minister Browne welcomed the proposed dialogue but maintained that the Caribbean's position on reparations remains unchanged. @wfwitness
